role: NESTED DEPENDENCY — interface abstraction only, NOT deep-profiled (third-party/first-party-sibling boundary)

phUSD.note: read by Antimatter.setPhUSD (145) and setPhUSDMinter (158) to prove wiring agreement

stablecoinConfigs.note: Antimatter destructures this 7-tuple at Antimatter.sol:284, taking index 0 (yieldStrategy) and index 2 (decimals) only. This IS the registered-decimals accessor — there is no dedicated decimalsOf(); getStablecoinConfig (265) is the struct-returning alternative.

asUsedByAntimatter.note: the deposit entry point — it is named `mint`, not depositStable. It mints phUSD to msg.sender (minter:232), i.e. to Antimatter, which is why Antimatter forwards at 261.

calculateMintAmountSemantics.capAwareVerdict: VERIFIED-BY-READING: NOT cap-aware. calculateMintAmount (243-256) reads only exchangeRate and decimals from the config; it never references maxMintPerDay, mintedToday, or lastMintTimestamp, and it is `view` so it cannot roll the window.
calculateMintAmountSemantics.enabledAwareNote: It also does not consult `enabled` or `paused`; it returns a non-zero quote for a disabled or unregistered stablecoin (unregistered => decimals 0, exchangeRate 0 => returns 0).
consequenceForTheNewExactEqualityCheck: The daily cap is enforced as a REVERT, not a haircut: minter:221 `require(config.mintedToday + phUSDAmount <= config.maxMintPerDay, 'Daily mint limit exceeded')`. It never mints a reduced amount. Therefore a cap over-run cannot produce a quote-vs-actual DIVERGENCE reaching Antimatter.sol:257 — the whole tx reverts inside minter.mint at line 251 first.
So Antimatter's cap exposure is availability (annihilate DoS once the daily budget is consumed), not a PhUSDAmountMismatch.
Likewise 'Stablecoin minting is paused' (minter:209) and 'Contract is paused' (minter:204) are reverts at Antimatter.sol:251, not mismatches.

Both Antimatter's quote (Antimatter.sol:234) and the minter's own internal quote (minter:212) call the SAME view with the SAME arguments inside the SAME transaction, and every input it reads (exchangeRate, decimals) is onlyOwner-mutable (updateExchangeRate minter:138, registerStablecoin minter:111). Divergence at Antimatter.sol:257 therefore requires either (a) a third party crediting phUSD to Antimatter during minter.mint, or (b) the minter/phUSD deviating from this code — i.e. it is a tripwire against a swapped or upgraded minter, not against normal operation. Not adjudicated here.
Rounding: the division by 1e18 at minter:255 truncates. Antimatter compares two truncations of the identical expression, so truncation is not itself a source of divergence.

dailyCapSurface.enforcement: minter:215-223, rolling 24h window keyed on block.timestamp >= lastMintTimestamp + 1 days; window resets to 0 and re-stamps on first mint after expiry
dailyCapSurface.defaultAtRegistration: maxMintPerDay: 0 (minter:125) => uncapped until the owner sets it
dailyCapSurface.readAccessor: none dedicated — read via the public stablecoinConfigs getter or getStablecoinConfig (265). Antimatter reads neither the cap nor the remaining budget.

otherSurface.note: max-approves the YS; PRECONDITION for minter.mint's YS deposit at 229 to succeed

trustBoundaryStatement: Antimatter treats PhusdStableMinter as the single source of truth for which stablecoins are supported, their decimals, and their exchange rate. Antimatter independently verifies only: (1) minter.phUSD() == its own phUSD, at configuration time (Antimatter.sol:145,158); (2) registered decimals == the token's own decimals (Antimatter.sol:292-295); (3) the stable fully left Antimatter (Antimatter.sol:254); (4) the phUSD received exactly equals the minter's pre-quote (Antimatter.sol:257). Everything else — that the deposit reached the yield strategy, that the exchange rate is economically correct, that the cap is set sanely — is ASSUMED.
